prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider._initialize() never restores token_expiry_time for tokens loaded from storage, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired token as valid and the proactive-refresh path is skipped, forcing a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider._initialize() never restores token_expiry_time for tokens loaded from storage, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired token as valid and the proactive-refresh path is skipped, forcing a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both target the same root cause. #1784 fixes it directly in _initialize() with a 4-line change that recomputes token_expiry_time via update_token_expiry(), and ships a dedicated expired_tokens test fixture. #2875's own added code comment attributes its 15-line reactive-refresh-on-401 workaround to this exact same bug ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time... Without this, every access-token expiry forces an interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh'). Once _initialize() is fixed, is_token_valid() correctly reports expiry and the existing proactive-refresh branch handles it, making #2875's downstream workaround unnecessary for the reported failure mode. The smaller, root-cause fix is sufficient on its own.

prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the SSE stream disconnects and reconnection with Last-Event-ID exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, _handle_reconnection currently just logs at debug level and returns — the in-flight request's caller is left waiting forever with no error ever delivered. Both PRs fix this same 'reconnection exhausted, caller never told' bug, just via different mechanisms: #2395 sends a JSONRPCError back through ctx.read_stream_writer for the specific pending request (session keeps running for everything else); #3098 instead adds a generic _unwrap_exception helper to dig a StreamableHTTPError out of an anyio ExceptionGroup and raise it, which surfaces failure by raising out of the transport rather than answering the pending JSON-RPC call. (2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing previously matched auth-param fields via naive substring/regex matching, which could false-positive on comma-separated values (e.g. quoted values containing commas, or one param name being a substring of another like 'error' vs 'error_description'). Both add a character-by-character tokenizer that walks the header respecting quoted strings and backslash escapes and splits only on top-level (unquoted) commas. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing previously matched auth-param fields via naive substring/regex matching, which could false-positive on comma-separated values (e.g. quoted values containing commas, or one param name being a substring of another like 'error' vs 'error_description'). Both add a character-by-character tokenizer that walks the header respecting quoted strings and backslash escapes and splits only on top-level (unquoted) commas. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both introduce nearly identical quote/escape-aware comma-splitting logic, but #3041 additionally scopes extraction to the specific auth scheme via `_extract_bearer_auth_params`, which partitions each comma-separated segment into scheme+remainder and only collects params following a 'Bearer' scheme token. #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` instead finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat param list, which does not disambiguate multiple challenges in a single WWW-Authenticate header (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="y"' per RFC 7235) - it would merge params from unrelated schemes. #3041's approach handles a case #3012's does not.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes any string value whose field annotation is not exactly `str`, so a field typed as a union that still allows a plain `str` (most commonly `str | None`) gets its string value wrongly parsed as JSON (e.g. a string that looks like a JSON object/array/bool gets corrupted into a dict/list/bool instead of staying a string). Both PRs change pre_parse_json's gating condition to skip pre-parsing in this situation. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes any string value whose field annotation is not exactly `str`, so a field typed as a union that still allows a plain `str` (most commonly `str | None`) gets its string value wrongly parsed as JSON (e.g. a string that looks like a JSON object/array/bool gets corrupted into a dict/list/bool instead of staying a string). Both PRs change pre_parse_json's gating condition to skip pre-parsing in this situation. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both patch the same call site (`isinstance(data_value, str) and <check>` in pre_parse_json), but the checks differ in correctness scope. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` skips pre-parsing whenever *every* member of a union is in a fixed 'simple type' set {str,int,float,bool,None}, without verifying that `str` is actually one of those members. That misfires on unions like `int | float`: neither member is str, yet the new check disables JSON pre-parsing anyway, so a JSON-encoded numeric string would no longer be decoded for that field — a regression on the pre-existing behavior for such unions. #3056's `_is_optional_str` only disables pre-parsing for the specific `str | None` shape (the one case where skipping is unambiguously safe), and also unwraps `Annotated[...]` before checking, so idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` parameters (the common FastMCP style) are covered too, which #2032 does not handle since it compares raw union args against a type frozenset without unwrapping Annotated.

clusters.pick_reason: Both introduce nearly identical quote/escape-aware comma-splitting logic, but #3041 additionally scopes extraction to the specific auth scheme via `_extract_bearer_auth_params`, which partitions each comma-separated segment into scheme+remainder and only collects params following a 'Bearer' scheme token. #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` instead finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat param list, which does not disambiguate multiple challenges in a single WWW-Authenticate header (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="y"' per RFC 7235) - it would merge params from unrelated schemes. #3041's approach handles a case #3012's does not.

clusters.pick_reason: Both patch the same call site (`isinstance(data_value, str) and <check>` in pre_parse_json), but the checks differ in correctness scope. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` skips pre-parsing whenever *every* member of a union is in a fixed 'simple type' set {str,int,float,bool,None}, without verifying that `str` is actually one of those members. That misfires on unions like `int | float`: neither member is str, yet the new check disables JSON pre-parsing anyway, so a JSON-encoded numeric string would no longer be decoded for that field — a regression on the pre-existing behavior for such unions. #3056's `_is_optional_str` only disables pre-parsing for the specific `str | None` shape (the one case where skipping is unambiguously safe), and also unwraps `Annotated[...]` before checking, so idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` parameters (the common FastMCP style) are covered too, which #2032 does not handle since it compares raw union args against a type frozenset without unwrapping Annotated.

clusters.pick_reason: Both introduce nearly identical quote/escape-aware comma-splitting logic, but #3041 additionally scopes extraction to the specific auth scheme via `_extract_bearer_auth_params`, which partitions each comma-separated segment into scheme+remainder and only collects params following a 'Bearer' scheme token. #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` instead finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat param list, which does not disambiguate multiple challenges in a single WWW-Authenticate header (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="y"' per RFC 7235) - it would merge params from unrelated schemes. #3041's approach handles a case #3012's does not.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing previously matched auth-param fields via naive substring/regex matching, which could false-positive on comma-separated values (e.g. quoted values containing commas, or one param name being a substring of another like 'error' vs 'error_description'). Both add a character-by-character tokenizer that walks the header respecting quoted strings and backslash escapes and splits only on top-level (unquoted) commas.
